To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sensitivity of dideoxynucleotide ‘Sanger’-sequencing is dramatically lower than that of massively parallel sequencing and pyrosequence, and that the latter two methods have comparable sensitivity.

dideoxy sequencing is not sensitive enough for clinical mutation diagnostics in lung cancer, whereas massively parallel sequencing is, and that histopathology is not reliable for stratification of tumor content and mutant allele frequency in tumor specimens.

massively parallel sequencing is the most sensitive method to detect clinically relevant EGFR mutations, and that the use of histological tumor content for stratification of clinical samples is questionable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the detection of the most sensitive mutations in the clinical lung tumor samples.
the development of novel diagnostic methods and the validation of established methods.
the molecular characterization of lung cancer and the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
massively parallel sequencing is the most reliable and sensitive technology to detect EGFR mutations in lung cancer patients.

the current clinical practice of using dideoxy sequencing for the detection of mutations in lung cancer patients for the decision to treat with EGFR inhibitors, is insufficient and should be reconsidered.
the current clinical practice of using dideoxy sequencing for EGFR mutation testing is inadequate and that the use of massively parallel sequencing is highly recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dideoxy sequencing and pyro sequencing are not sensitive enough and should not be used to determine the EGFR mutation status in patients with non-small cell lung cancers.
massively parallel sequencing should be the gold standard for mutation detection in lung cancer.
massively parallel sequencing is the most sensitive and accurate method for mutation diagnostics in clinical samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sensitivity of the analytical method used is critical for correct stratification of patients for EGFR inhibitor treatment and that massively parallel sequencing is currently the most sensitive method available.
the most sensitive mutation-detection technology, massively parallel sequencing, is also the most accurate.

massively parallel sequencing is the gold standard for the detection of somatic mutations in cancer and that other technologies, including dideoxy sequencing and pyro-sequencing, should only be used if the results of massively parallel sequencing are not available.
